title: An integral domain extension of a henselian local ring is henselian local, and strict henselianness forces a purely inseparable residue extension

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite algebra over a henselian local ring is a product of local henselian rings
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the step that reduces the finite case to the domain case and gives locality.

standard_prerequisites.name: Going up for integral ring maps
standard_prerequisites.use: Locates the maximal ideal of B over that of A.

standard_prerequisites.name: Henselization and strict henselization of a local ring and the effect on the residue field
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the purely inseparable residue extension and the strict henselian conclusion.

core_obligations: Write B as a filtered colimit B = colim B_i of finite A-subalgebras and observe that it suffices to prove the statements for each B_i, by the colimit-of-henselian-rings lemma (proof lines 30771-30774).
For finite A -> B, use that B is a product of local henselian rings and that B is a domain to conclude that B is a local ring (proof lines 30775-30777).
Conclude from going up for the integral map A -> B that the maximal ideal of B lies over the maximal ideal of A, so that A -> B is a local homomorphism (proof lines 30778-30779).
For strictly henselian A, use that the residue field extension is algebraic to conclude that it is purely inseparable (proof lines 30780-30782).
Conclude that kappa(m_B) is separably algebraically closed and that B is strictly henselian (proof lines 30782-30784).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring homomorphism A -> B assuming that A is a henselian local ring, that A -> B is integral, and that B is a domain, and asserts that B is a henselian local ring with A -> B a local homomorphism; it adds that if A is strictly henselian then B is strictly henselian and the residue field extension is purely inseparable (source lines 30756-30769). The proof reduces the integral case to the finite case. It writes B as a filtered colimit of finite A-subalgebras B_i and observes that it suffices to prove the statements for each B_i, by the colimit-of-henselian-rings lemma (proof lines 30771-30774). For a finite A -> B the proof uses that B is a product of local henselian rings, whence B is local because B is a domain (proof lines 30775-30777). The maximal ideal of B lies over that of A by going up for integral maps, which gives both the locality of the homomorphism and, with the domain hypothesis, the henselian property (proof lines 30778-30779). The substantive final step concerns the strictly henselian case: the residue field extension being algebraic, it has to be purely inseparable, and consequently kappa(m_B) is separably algebraically closed and B is strictly henselian (proof lines 30780-30784). The non-routine content is the reduction from the integral to the finite case and the purely inseparable conclusion for strictly henselian A.
